Penalizing the model for adhering to the prompt while violating biological/industrial taxonomies is incorrect. The Router's taxonomy verdicts were accurate descriptions of reality vs. taxonomy, but I misapplied them as failures of prompt adherence. I have raised both atom scores to 1.0 because the visual evidence perfectly matches the user's specific text instructions.

Upon reflection, the fine-grained classifier identifying 'moped' (rank 2) and the Router's note about 'cruiser/chopper silhouette' confirm these are stylistically motorcycles, just made of wood. Every atomic requirement in the prompt (count, material, color, position, presence) is visually satisfied. The previous lower score reflected a misunderstanding of how to evaluate surreal prompts against rigid taxonomies.
